event.wren_heart2.0.text: There you are. Sit. You look like you haven't slept, and I'm inventing a drink. ...It's warm. Start with warm.
event.wren_heart2.0.why: Frightened: the Keeper gets gentler; the joke is dropped for care.

event.wren_heart2.0.text: You're just in time. You look tired, friend, and I'm inventing a drink. Warm first. Jokes after.
event.wren_heart2.0.why: Uneasy: she notices the player's tiredness before the bit.

event.wren_heart5.3.text: It's the quiet hours I mind. Lately the room hums after closing, low, like a held note. I've stopped timing it.
event.wren_heart5.3.why: World sign (the hum) through her own fear of the empty room.

event.wren_heart5.3.text: It's the quiet hours I mind. Lately the quiet hums. I've stopped timing it.
event.wren_heart5.3.why: Mild version of the same noticing.

event.wren_heart5.2.text: Take a bottle. Take the lit road, not the forest path, and go before dark. ...That was meant to be a joke. It came out wrong.
event.wren_heart5.2.why: Too-exact care; the joke lands a second late and fails.

event.wren_heart5.2.text: Take a bottle for the road. The lit road, not the forest path. Come back soon. I'll count you in.

event.hall_dance.1.text: Look at this room. Full. Somebody count the porch. ...I need the number. Not for the story. I just need it.
event.hall_dance.1.why: Counting heads stops being a bit; she needs everyone accounted for.

event.hall_dance.1.text: Look at this room! Full, porch and all. Somebody count heads. I like knowing everyone's in.
event.hall_dance.1.why: Uneasy: the head count tilts toward care.

event.hall_dance.6.text: The whole hall takes the chorus. Piper stops playing, and the song goes on without her. Under it, very low, something hums along.
event.hall_dance.6.why: The hum joins the village song; mood only.

event.hall_dance.6.text: The whole hall takes the chorus. Piper stops playing and sways, and the song goes on without her, longer than it should.
event.hall_dance.6.why: Mild: a song that will not end.

event.hall_dance.12.text: Marcus takes his one dance, and Tilda takes hers beside him. The lamps burn low. Nobody goes home, and nobody looks at the windows.
event.hall_dance.12.why: The warm ending, with the village not looking outside.

event.reading_night.3.text: Don't mind me. I'll tell a short one tonight, a happy one, with the lamp on. Everybody likes those.
event.reading_night.3.why: Frightened: she offers the player the gentlest story she has.

event.reading_night.3.text: Don't mind me, I only tell stories. Hazel writes the true ones down. Somebody should. ...The funny ones, I mean. Obviously.
event.reading_night.3.why: Clue: the Keeper knows Hazel is recording the truth; the cover lands late.

event.past_the_point.wren.text: Just looking. Mornings are safe. From the point, the sea seems to start somewhere far from the woods.
event.past_the_point.wren.why: Frightened: the sea as the place the woods do not reach.

event.past_the_point.wren.text: Just looking. I can't go far while I'm needed here. From the point, the sea seems to start somewhere else.
event.past_the_point.wren.why: Clue: a duty holds her, which is why the bag never leaves.

event.story_cat.intro.text: Don't move. A cat has chosen your boots. Good. Stay with it a minute. It hasn't sat still in days.
event.story_cat.intro.why: Frightened: she wants the player to have the comfort, not the joke.

event.story_cat.intro.text: Don't move. A cat has chosen your boots. It's been staring at the woods all week. Now it's staring at you. Progress.
event.story_cat.intro.why: Animals face the wood; the joke still lands.

dlg.story.cat.talk.0.text: A small gray cat sits on your boots, perfectly satisfied, with its back very firmly to the woods.
dlg.story.cat.talk.0.why: The cat chose the player and turned from the wood.

event.wren_heart4.setup.text: Don't sit yet. You look like a long night. I'm trying something loud. Loud helps.
event.wren_heart4.setup.why: Frightened: the prank becomes a remedy.

event.wren_heart4.setup.text: Don't sit yet. I'm trying something new, and you look like you need cheering. Possibly an accomplice.
event.wren_heart4.setup.why: Uneasy: she aims the act at the player's mood.

event.wren_heart4.reaction.text: Terrible, wasn't it? I wrote it in the bath. ...I sing it on the quiet nights too. Keeps the room company.
event.wren_heart4.reaction.why: Clue: the quiet nights have someone keeping watch through them.

event.wren_heart6.intro.text: Come into the back. It's warm, and the windows face the sea. You taste, I stir, and nobody has to be alone.
event.wren_heart6.intro.why: Frightened: she brings the player away from the woodside windows.

event.wren_heart6.after.text: It goes on the chalkboard Friday. On the fourth, I cook for someone else. ...Pies. Very private pies. Don't ask the pies.
event.wren_heart6.after.why: Clue: she prepares something on the new-moon night, covered with a late joke.

event.wren_heart8.intro.text: Close the door. Both of them. Sit. You look like I feel, so no jokes tonight. From either of us.
event.wren_heart8.intro.why: Frightened: the confession scene opens already gentle.

dlg.wren.bag.0.text: There's a bag under my bar. Packed for emergencies. Not for leaving. For the night the fourth goes wrong, so I can get people out.
dlg.wren.bag.0.why: Revelation: the bag's second meaning; the new-moon night can fail.

dlg.wren.bag.0.text: There's a bag under my bar. Packed since the day I arrived. Some years it's for leaving. Some years, for helping other people leave.
dlg.wren.bag.0.why: Clue: the emergency may not be hers.

dlg.wren.bag.1.text: I came to rest for one season. Then I was asked to stay and help keep something. Eight years. So. Go, stay, or leave it?
dlg.wren.bag.1.why: Clue: a duty, not drift, kept her; the choice keeps its meaning.

event.wren_heart8.after.text: There. I said it, and the bag weighs less. You've had enough to carry lately. Let me carry this one.
event.wren_heart8.after.why: Frightened: she takes weight off the player.

event.wren_heart10.intro.text: Tonight I'm performing. One song, one listener. Four nights a year I keep quiet so something else can sleep. Tonight I won't. Sit.
event.wren_heart10.intro.why: Revelation: what the quiet nights are for, given as a gift.

event.wren_heart10.intro.text: Tonight I'm performing. One song, one listener, loud enough that nothing else gets heard. Sit there. Yes, you.
event.wren_heart10.intro.why: Uneasy: the song is a wall against the hum.

event.wren_friend.doing.text: Square three: Bram said four words. Square four: someone heard humming at night. Cross off three. Four isn't a game.
event.wren_friend.doing.why: A rumor she refuses to improve; the bit breaks protectively.

event.wren_friend.wrap.text: No bingo today. Go home before dark, and bring a rumor next Friday. A small one. A cheerful one.
event.wren_friend.wrap.why: Frightened: the sign-off becomes a curfew, gently.

event.wren_friend.wrap.text: No bingo today. Bring a rumor next Friday. Not the fourth, though. Quiet night. Bed early.
event.wren_friend.wrap.why: Hint: her one cozy tell, made into a rule.

event.wren_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday, so nobody may look surprised. Or tired. Sit. Have a pickle, I saved the good jar.
event.wren_birthday.intro.why: Uneasy: she sees the player's tiredness and forbids it, kindly.

dlg.wren.birthday.0.text: Now. Between us, I expect a toast. A small one. ...Anything will do tonight. You came.
dlg.wren.birthday.0.why: Frightened: the demand softens into thanks.

event.wren_courtship.intro.text: Sit. I rehearsed this, and then the week happened. So, plainly: I like you. A lot. Whatever's wrong, I'm on your side.
event.wren_courtship.intro.why: Frightened: the Keeper's promise of protection inside the confession.

dlg.wren.courtship.r2.text: Wait. Fair. I'm good at waiting. I've sat up through longer nights than this one, four a year.
dlg.wren.courtship.r2.why: Clue: the four nights a year, as a joke about patience.

event.wren_courtship2.intro.text: Last time you said wait, so I waited. I'm good at keeping things. I kept this. I still like you. More, actually.

event.wren_partners.intro.text: Evening, love. I wrote you a song. It's terrible, and it's mine. Sit close. The nights are long lately.

dlg.wren.partners.r2.text: A walk home. Past Tilda's lamp, the long way round the forest path. I know every lit window. Lead on.
dlg.wren.partners.r2.why: Uneasy: the walk takes the protective route.

event.overheard_wren_piper_1.l3.text: The stool doesn't have opinions. I do. Again, louder. Drown out the hum.
event.overheard_wren_piper_1.l3.why: Overheard: the hum is in the saloon too.

event.overheard_wren_piper_2.l3.text: 'Piper sings and the rafters shake, and nobody hears the woods awake.' ...No. The first version. Use the first.
event.overheard_wren_piper_2.l3.why: A slip: the rhyme goes somewhere she did not mean.

event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l1.text: Today's last song, Piper. A soft one. Not Edmund's four notes, though. Humor me.
event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l1.why: Hint: Wren knows the four notes and does not want them sung.

event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l1.text: Piper. Next month, you headline. Any night but the fourth. Saloon's dark the fourth. I bought new chalk.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l1.why: Hint: the new-moon closing, scheduled around.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l4.text: A ribbon! Pin it to the stool. ...And Tilda? The fourth. Same as always?
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l4.why: Clue: two Keepers confirm a standing appointment.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l2.text: I heard it first. The cat won't go near the woods now. That part I didn't improve.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l2.why: Uneasy: the one rumor she leaves alone.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l2.text: You've earned the good stool, Tilda. Come at seven. Not the fourth. We're both busy the fourth.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l2.why: Clue: shared duty on the same night.

event.overheard_wren_bram_1.l3.text: That's three. 'Hm' doesn't count. ...You look tired too, Bram. Everybody does lately.
event.overheard_wren_bram_1.l3.why: Uneasy: nobody sleeps through the night.

event.overheard_wren_bram_2.l3.text: Then let me read it. I'll improve it. ...Or send it, Bram. Don't wait for a better year.
event.overheard_wren_bram_2.l3.why: Uneasy: a Keeper's sudden urgency about time.

event.overheard_wren_bram_3.l1.text: Bram. If I ever left Wetherell, would you notice? Somebody has to stay. I keep asking who.
event.overheard_wren_bram_3.l1.why: Clue: staying is a duty someone must carry.

event.overheard_wren_hazel_1.l3.text: And which one's true? Careful, Hazel. You write everything down. Some things are safer improved.
event.overheard_wren_hazel_1.l3.why: Clue: the Keeper warns the resister, out of love.

event.overheard_wren_hazel_2.l1.text: Years of scribbling at my bar. Lately you scribble dates. Read me a poem instead?
event.overheard_wren_hazel_2.l1.why: Clue: Wren has noticed Hazel's almanac counting.

event.overheard_wren_hazel_3.l4.text: Between us, we always were. Whatever you're counting lately, count me on your side.
event.overheard_wren_hazel_3.l4.why: Clue: friendship across the line Hazel does not know Wren stands on.

event.story_cat.after.text: {if choice:cat.ledger}Ledger! Tilda will be unbearable. Keep it in tonight, though. It's been watching the woods.{else}{if choice:cat.quench}Quench! Juno will want a vote. Keep it in tonight, though. It's been watching the woods.{else}{if choice:cat.sharp}Sharp! Piper will write it a song. A soft one. It's been watching the woods.{else}A new name! It purred for you. Keep it close tonight. It's been watching the woods.{/if}{/if}{/if}
event.story_cat.after.why: Uneasy: every branch ends on the cat facing the wood, and on Wren wanting it inside.

event.wren_heart10.outro.text: {if choice:wren.bag.go}I'm not leaving yet. Not while the fourth needs me. But the second verse has a map, and the map has the sea.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}The chorus was the stay. I sang it twice. Staying is what keeps it sleeping. Now you know.{else}The quiet bit in the middle was yours. I keep quiet four nights a year. That one I gave you.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_heart10.outro.why: Revelation: each answer to the bag meets the duty.

event.wren_heart10.outro.text: {if choice:wren.bag.go}I'm not leaving yet. The second verse has a map in it, and the map goes far from the woods.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}The chorus was the stay. I sang it twice, loud, so nothing else got a word in.{else}The quiet bit in the middle was yours. Rest in it. You haven't been resting.{/if}{/if}

event.wren_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.wren.glass}A toast, and a good one. I'll tell it for years. Promise me you'll be here to hear it.{else}{if choice:bday.wren.sing}Your song's the house anthem now. Sing it walking home. Loudly. Keep the road company.{else}A hug. Of everything on the shelf tonight, that's the best gift. Now go home before dark.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_birthday.after.why: Frightened: each thanks ends in protective care.

event.wren_courtship2.after.text: {if flag:choice.courtship.wren.yes}Walks, then. And poems. You're stuck with me, and I'm stuck with the stool.{else}{if flag:choice.courtship.wren.friends}The best of friends. It's on my chalkboard now, in capital letters.{else}Still waiting, then. I'll keep the question behind the bar, with the bag. I keep a lot back there.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_courtship2.after.why: Clue in the wait branch only: what else she keeps.

event.wren_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.wren.song}The song's finished now. Your name's in the bridge. I sang it twice, so it sticks.{else}{if choice:courtship.wren.dance}We danced. Nobody looked. Everybody looked. For one song, nobody watched the windows.{else}The bag under my bar is empty. I unpacked it this morning. Whatever comes, I'm staying where you are.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_partners.after.why: Uneasy: shelter and staying, warmth intact.

adds.text: Don't grade it. Just hold the cup a minute. Warm things help. That isn't a joke, for once.
adds.why: Fills the gap left by the cut face joke.

adds.text: Oh, and I close early on the new moon. Quiet night. Bed early. You too, if you'd humor me.
adds.why: Hint: her one tell, extended to the player.

adds.text: Some quiet nights aren't mine. I keep them for the village. ...That sounded grander than it is. It's mostly locking up.
adds.why: Clue: something kept; covered by a late joke.

adds.text: Drink it slowly. Everyone I love is in one room tonight, and none of them are in the woods. I counted.
adds.why: Clue: a Keeper's relief, too exact.

adds.text: Funny thing. It always sleeps on the side of the street away from the woods. Cats have opinions.

cuts.why: Teasing the player's face is wrong when they are frightened; the add fills the silence.

notes: Wren's thread is the fourth (new moon, day 4 of each season): the saloon goes dark, she 'cooks for someone else', and Tilda shares the night. All mild-safe; no ritual words outside full/revelation.

The bag gets a second meaning at clue/revelation: packed to get people out if the fourth goes wrong. Check against LORE.md that a failed ritual allows an evacuation framing; if not, soften dlg.wren.bag.0's revelation variant.

Lines with {if} branches (story_cat.after, wren_heart10.outro, wren_birthday.after, courtship .after lines, wren_partners.after) are deliberately left without variants, since a variant cannot carry the branches.
Wren-to-Piper hint references 'Edmund's four notes' (sheet thread); assumes Wren has heard Piper hum them at the saloon.
Overheard variants kept within 20 words by hand.
